This is the complete format of `theme.json`. The tables are made from the [published JSON Schema](/schemas/v1/theme.json) when the
site is built, so they list every key the deck reads; the text between them explains how the keys work together. To make a theme
from scratch start with [a theme in five minutes](/docs/themes/quick-start/), and to see keys at work look at the
[cookbook](/docs/cookbook/).

## How a theme file is read

Every value is optional and **absent means off** for the newer keys, or the default theme's value for the original ones.

- **Merging.** A value you leave out comes from `default-dark`. Some groups are never taken from it, because a theme that does
  not mention them should not get them: `colors.ramp`, `colors.cardTints`, `colors.backgroundPalette`, `pattern`, `background`,
  `icons`, `meta`, every card chrome value (shape, fill gradient, border style, dashes, gradient and animation, highlight,
  sheen, accent strip, corner marks, shadow, glow, tint, compact), `typography.valueFill` and `valueGlow`, and every gauge value
  except `style`. The rest merge key by key.
- **An invalid value** is replaced by the default (for an optional value, by "absent") and one warning in `urdeck.log` names the
  theme, the key and the value. A number outside its range, a colour that does not parse, a name that is not listed, a value of
  the wrong kind and a list with a bad item are all invalid. A bad item drops the whole list, except in `card.cutCorners` and
  `card.cornerMarks.corners`, where an unknown name is dropped and the others stay. Names are read in any case. A file that is
  not valid JSON makes the theme unavailable.
- **Units.** Sizes are fractions of one grid cell (a quarter of the screen's width), angles are degrees (0 is left to right,
  clockwise), times are seconds, tracking is in em, and colours are `#RRGGBB` or `#AARRGGBB`, alpha first.
- **Unknown keys** are allowed and ignored, so a theme with a key this deck does not read still loads. `urdeck-cli theme validate`
  warns about the key (`THEME002`) and suggests the nearest one when you misspell it.

Rules between values are checked after each value on its own, and each warns once and changes only what it names:

- A `card.borderStyle`, `borderGradient` or `borderAnimate` with a border width of 0 has no effect (`THEME050`).
- `card.borderAnimate` with `mode` `spin` needs a `borderGradient` of kind `conic`; without one the animation is off (`THEME051`).
- `card.borderAnimate` on a `dashed` border is not drawn (`THEME057`): the deck moves the border as a ring stretched round
  the card, which a dash pattern fitted to each side does not survive. The border stays still.
- A `pattern.spacing` under three times `pattern.thickness` makes the marks run together (`THEME052`).
- Corner marks with an `inset` below 0 reach outside the card; with a `card.gap` smaller than that they would overlap the next
  card (`THEME053`).
- `card.shape` `chamfer` with `card.compact.shape` `circle` is allowed; the circle applies to compact cards only.
- More than one continuous animation is allowed and written to the log at information level (`THEME090`).

## The file

<SchemaTable schema="v1/theme.json" path="$schema" />

## `meta`

<SchemaTable schema="v1/theme.json" path="meta" />

`meta` describes the theme to an editor and never affects what the deck draws. A theme is listed by an editor only if it has a
`name`, a `description` and a `mode` (`THEME080`).

## `colors`

<SchemaTable schema="v1/theme.json" path="colors" />

A gauge draws its fill in `colors.accent`, or in `colors.warning` or `colors.critical` once its reading has reached that level,
and its track in the same colour at the alpha of `colors.accentDim`. A reading that is not current (stale, pending, unavailable)
uses `colors.textMuted` for both. The number keeps `colors.text`, except where it lies over the fill of a vertical bar: there it
is `colors.text` or `colors.background`, whichever contrasts more with the fill.

### The background palette

The built-in [background](/docs/backgrounds/) shaders draw with four colours that come from the theme. `colors.backgroundPalette`
sets them. It is the one value that is not taken from `default-dark`: a light theme would get a dark palette. A theme without
it gets a palette made from its own colours instead, `colors.background` mixed towards `colors.accent` by 0, 20, 40 and 60 %.
Keep the palette dark and low in contrast unless the theme's cards are opaque: a bright, busy background under translucent
cards makes their text hard to read. The `colors` of the `background` setting in the configuration win over both.

## `card`

The card is what each widget sits on.

<SchemaTable schema="v1/theme.json" path="card" />

- **Shape.** `round` is the rounded rectangle of `card.radius`, limited to half the card's smaller side. `chamfer` cuts the
  corners named in `cutCorners` with a straight line `cut` long along each side, limited to half the smaller side; the other
  corners are square and `radius` is not used. An empty `cutCorners` gives square cards. The widget's content is clipped to the
  shape.
- **Fill**, the first that applies: `fillGradient` (linear across the card at its angle, the colours evenly spaced), `tint`
  `cycle` with `colors.cardTints`, `colors.cardFill`. Without `cardTints` a tinted theme uses the card fill. The text colour does
  not change with the tint.
- **Tint order.** A card takes the tint at its index, counting round the list. The index is its place among its page's placed,
  visible cards, row by row and then column by column, from the first tint on every page. A dock slot takes its position in the
  dock.
- **Border**, always inside the card's edge, `card.borderWidth` wide: `solid`, `none`, or `dashed` with `borderDash`. A dashed
  border has a dash centred on every corner; on each side the dash and the gap are scaled together so a whole number of them
  fits. `borderGradient` colours the border, solid or dashed: `linear` at its angle, `conic` once round the card's centre,
  starting at the right. A border width of 0 draws nothing.
- **Animated border.** `spin` turns the conic `borderGradient` once round the card every `period` seconds (7 when absent);
  `pulse` breathes the border's opacity between full and 0.55 and back, for a solid, linear or conic border. Both move in 15
  steps a second over a card that is never repainted for them, at about 3 % of one CPU core for eight cards. The border moves
  only at the [motion level](/docs/themes/motion/) `full`, while the display is on and the deck is shown; otherwise it is the still
  border, drawn exactly as a border without `borderAnimate`.
- **Hairlines.** In a theme that sets any card value other than the radius, border width, gap and padding, a border of 2 pixels or less is drawn at a whole number of
  pixels, never under 1; under one pixel it is written to `urdeck.log` once (`THEME055`). The highlight, strip and mark
  thicknesses are hairlines too.
- **Highlight.** `highlight.top` and `highlight.bottom` draw a line `thickness` wide just inside the top or bottom edge, round the
  corners with the edge, fading to transparent over the first and last eighth of the card's width. It is drawn after the
  widget's content, so content never covers it.
- **Sheen.** A radial light centred at `x` times the card's width and `y` times its height, reaching `size` times the card's
  width, from `color` to transparent; over the fill, under the content.
- **Accent strip.** A line `thickness` wide along `side`, inside the card, `length` times the side long and centred on it, over
  the fill and under the content. Its colour is the entry of `colors` at the card's index (the same index as the tint). `fade`
  fades it from its colour at the start to transparent at the end. `glow` lays a blurred copy under it.
- **Corner marks.** `bracket` draws an L at each corner in `corners`, one arm along each edge; `tick` draws one arm, along the top
  or bottom edge. Each arm is `size` long from the mark's outer corner and `thickness` wide. `inset` is the distance from the
  card's edge to the mark's outer edge: positive moves the mark in, negative puts it partly or wholly outside the card (minus half
  the thickness puts the line across the edge). Marks are drawn after the content, so content never covers them.
- **Shadow and glow.** The shadow is the card's shape moved by `x` and `y`, grown by `spread` on every side, blurred by `blur`,
  in `color`. The glow blurs the card's shape outwards by `blur`. Both, and the outside part of the corner marks, are drawn under
  all the cards of the page, so they never cover a card's content, and each card's own shape is cut out of its own shadow and
  glow, so a translucent card does not show them through its fill. They take no input, and a pressed card's shadow shrinks and
  dims with the card.
- **Translucent cards.** When a card fill colour has some transparency, a neighbour's shadow would show through the card. The
  shadow's offset and blur, and the glow's blur, are then scaled down together until they reach no further than `card.gap` past the
  card; `urdeck.log` says so once. A theme with opaque cards keeps its full reach (`THEME054` tells you in advance).
- **Compact cards.** A dock slot and a page card of one grid cell (1x1) are compact; every other card is not. A compact card takes
  `card.compact` in place of the page card's values, each on its own: `radius`, `borderWidth` and `shape` replace the page's, and
  a value `compact` does not set is the page card's. `compact.accentStrip` and `compact.cornerMarks` are merged key by key over
  the page's. A `circle` is a rounded card of half its smaller side as the radius: a circle on a square card, a capsule on one that
  is not square (`THEME056`). The padding is not overridden. A widget in the dock is given a theme with the compact corner radius
  and border width; a 1x1 widget on a page is given the page's theme, so only its card is compact.

## `pattern`

<SchemaTable schema="v1/theme.json" path="pattern" />

- **Kinds.** `dots` (round dots of radius `thickness`), `grid` (horizontal and vertical lines; with `majorEvery`, every
  `majorEvery`-th line in each direction, starting with the first, takes `major`), `hatch` (parallel lines, `spacing` apart
  across the lines) and `scanlines` (horizontal lines). The first mark is half a repeat in from the top and left edges.
- **The angle** of a `hatch` is in degrees from horizontal, positive rising to the right: 45 (the default) runs from bottom left
  to top right, 0 or 180 is horizontal and 90 or -90 vertical. `angle` is used by `hatch` only, `majorEvery` and `major` by `grid`
  only.
- **Whole pixels.** The distance between marks is the spacing in pixels rounded to a whole pixel (at least 2), a line is a whole
  number of pixels wide (at least 1) and a dot's radius is at least half a pixel. A hatch's angle is adjusted by under one degree
  so its lines meet across every repeat. On the 1100 pixel wide panel Carbon's dots are 35 pixels apart.
- **Where.** One texture over the whole window: above the background, its scrim and the theme's background colour, under every
  card, the dock and the page indicator. It does not slide with the pages, takes no input and is drawn whatever the configuration's
  `background` is, `none` included, because it belongs to the theme.
- **Cost.** The pattern is drawn once per theme and window size into one small block of whole repeats and laid out as tiles;
  nothing is repainted while the deck runs.

## `divider`

The rule widgets draw between their sections. A theme with no `divider` gets the rule the weather card always drew.

<SchemaTable schema="v1/theme.json" path="divider" />

## `typography`

<SchemaTable schema="v1/theme.json" path="typography" />

- **Fonts per role.** `fonts.value`, `fonts.unit` and `fonts.label` name a family or a file in the theme folder for that role; a
  role without one, and the body and title, use `typography.font`. A role whose font cannot be loaded falls back one step at a
  time: the role's font, `typography.font`, the default theme's font (Inter), the system font. Each missing font is one warning per
  loaded theme. A file path that leaves the theme folder is refused. See [fonts and licences](/docs/themes/fonts/).
- **Weights the font cannot make.** A weight outside a variable font's weight axis is drawn at the nearest end of the axis, and a
  weight on a single-weight file is drawn at the file's own weight; each is one warning per role per loaded theme (`THEME023`).
  An installed family is not checked.
- **Optical size.** `off` leaves the axis where the font puts it. `auto` sets it for each role whose font has the axis: the top of
  the axis (the display cut) for values and units, which are drawn large, and the role's size in pixels, limited to the axis, for
  labels, body and titles. A Didone such as Bodoni Moda needs it for its hairlines at large sizes.
- **Case** applies to a readout's label and to a text line at the label step (`case.label`) and at the title step
  (`case.title`). Body text and values are never recased.
- **Tracking** is added after each character but the last, in em: `value` to a readout's value (the digits keep their equal widths
  and the spacing is part of the fit, so the size does not change with the value), `label` to labels and label lines, `title` to
  title lines. Body text and units are not spaced.
- **`slant`** leans a readout's value to the right about its baseline. The top of a slanted value reaches past the rectangle's
  right edge by the slant's tangent times the cap height.
- **`valueScale`** multiplies the size a widget asks of a readout, and the result is never larger than the size at which the
  value, unit and label fill the rectangle. Above 1 it enlarges only a readout a widget draws smaller than it could (a gauge's
  readout, a clock set below full size); below 1 it shrinks every readout.
- **`valueFill`** fills a readout's value with the gradient across the value's box; a stale reading or a colour the widget gives
  the value replaces the gradient. **`valueGlow`** draws a blurred copy behind the value.

The split-flap clock's digits, a gauge's own centre text and an image tile's letter take the role's font and optical size, but not
the case, spacing, slant, fill or glow.

## `gauge`

<SchemaTable schema="v1/theme.json" path="gauge" />

A value that does not apply to the gauge's style is ignored without a warning. A `meter` and a `thickbar` put the readout above
the track, left-aligned, and so does a `bar` with `layout` `stacked`. A `tach` has ticks (28, every fourth longer) and a redline
from 0.85 even when the theme sets none. A group the theme writes takes defaults for the keys it leaves out: ticks 11 marks,
every fifth longer, 0.04 long and 0.006 thick; redline from 0.85; marker a diamond 0.05 across. Tick numbers run 0 to 100.
`labelPosition` `below` and `above` apply to arcs. The track is cut into blocks like the fill when `segments` is set.

`gauge.style` is the shape a gauge takes when a widget asks for "the theme's"; `plain` is not allowed here (a gauge that draws no
shape is no gauge), and an unknown name falls back to `ring` with a warning. A widget's own explicit style wins.

## `indicator`

The page indicator (see [pages and the dock](/docs/pages-and-dock/#pages)). A theme written before it existed takes all of these
from `default-dark`, with no warning.

<SchemaTable schema="v1/theme.json" path="indicator" />

## `press`

How a card looks while a finger is down on a widget that accepts taps. The whole card, border included, is scaled around its
centre and dimmed by the compositor; the widget is not repainted. `scale` must be between 0.5 and 1 and `opacity` between 0.1 and
1; a value outside that is replaced by the default's with a warning. Set both to 1 to switch the feedback off. How fast the card
moves is not a theme value.

<SchemaTable schema="v1/theme.json" path="press" />

## `dock`

The dock (see [pages and the dock](/docs/pages-and-dock/#the-dock)). `height` is the height of the band reserved for it at the
bottom of the screen, and also the side of a dock slot: the theme's sizes are applied to a slot as they are to a grid cell, so a
docked card is a miniature whose corners, padding and text shrink with this value. It must be between 0.2 and 1. The built-in
themes use 0.71, which on the 1100x3840 panel fits under the thirteenth row together with the page indicator, so the dock costs
no row there; a larger value takes a row.

<SchemaTable schema="v1/theme.json" path="dock" />

## `icons`

<SchemaTable schema="v1/theme.json" path="icons" />

The weather card draws its condition icons from the set, and the shortcut card its `theme:` glyphs and the fallback glyph for an
icon that cannot be found. A theme that names a set gets static outline icons, drawn in the theme's stroke and tint, in place of
the animated colour icons. There is no `animated` key: icons from a set are pictures. How to make a set is on the
[icon sets](/docs/themes/icons/) page.

## `background`

What the deck shows behind the cards when the configuration has no `background` of its own. See
[theme backgrounds](/docs/backgrounds/#theme-backgrounds) for the order (the user's choice, `none` included, then `default`,
then `static`, then `colors.background`) and for what happens when one fails.

<SchemaTable schema="v1/theme.json" path="background" />

## `motion`

<SchemaTable schema="v1/theme.json" path="motion" />

At `full` the theme's continuous animations run; at `reduced` and `off` none does, and each is drawn as it is when still. See
[motion](/docs/themes/motion/).
